DOCS-VERIFICATION 2026-06-07: (1) trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html — FILTER (WHERE ...) clause on aggregate functions CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'The FILTER keyword can be used to remove rows from aggregation processing with a condition expressed using a WHERE clause.' Syntax `aggregate_function(...) FILTER (WHERE <condition>)` is valid Trino 467. Example `SUM(x) FILTER (WHERE condition)` shown verbatim. (2) Same page — MULTIPLE aggregate functions in a SINGLE SELECT over the SAME row set CONFIRMED supported: docs demonstrate grouping queries with multiple aggregates over one dataset; conditional `CASE` aggregates and `FILTER` clauses can co-exist on different aggregates targeting the same rows. Therefore the single-pass form `SUM(CASE WHEN cond THEN x ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(x)` and the FILTER form `SUM(x) FILTER (WHERE cond) * 100.0 / SUM(x)` are both valid Trino 467 idioms over the same FROM-list rows in ONE SELECT. (3) Column-scope rule = universal SQL semantics: a CTE or subquery in the FROM list exposes ONLY its projected SELECT-list columns to the outer query; base columns of underlying tables are NOT carried through — once aggregated to a single alias, only that alias is visible above. Confirmed by Trino's standard SQL conformance — referencing a base column at the outer level that the inner CTE/subquery did not project produces a column-not-found error at planning.
